papers.title: Effect of internal defects on the compression behavior of stainless steel lattice structure fabricated by selective laser melting
papers.first_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Superlight Materials & Surface Technology, Ministry of Education, College of Materials Science and Chemical Engineering, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin 150001, PR China

corresponding_authors.name: Jiandong Wang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Key Laboratory of Superlight Materials & Surface Technology, Ministry of Education, College of Materials Science and Chemical Engineering, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin 150001, PR China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM不锈钢点阵结构的内部缺陷对压缩性能的影响，但与生物医学植入物的应力屏蔽或骨整合无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not link lattice structure to implant stress shielding or osseointegration, uses stainless steel instead of biomedical-grade Ti alloys, and does not include fatigue testing or surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究内部缺陷对SLM不锈钢点阵结构压缩性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过实验表征缺陷并比较有缺陷与无缺陷结构的压缩响应。
summary_zh.result: 内部缺陷显著降低点阵结构的压缩强度和刚度。
summary_zh.validation: 通过扫描电镜和压缩实验验证缺陷表征和力学性能。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the influence of internal defects on the compressive behavior of stainless steel lattice structures fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Defects were characterized using microscopy, and the compression response of defective and defect-free structures was compared.
summary_en.result: Internal defects significantly reduce the compressive strength and stiffness of the lattice structures.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through SEM imaging and mechanical compression tests.

papers.title: In-situ reinforced Ti6Al4V-TiB2 titanium matrix composite fabricated by selective laser melting: Microstructure, mechanical properties and heat treatment

corresponding_authors.name: Shun Guo
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Key Laboratory of Controlled Arc Intelligent Additive Manufacturing Technology, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Nanjing, 210094, China

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Ti6Al4V-TiB2复合材料的SLM制备及力学性能，但与生物医学应用中的应力屏蔽、疲劳、表面粗糙度或骨整合无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address stress shielding, fatigue behavior, surface roughness, as-built morphology, or osseointegration; it focuses solely on static mechanical properties and microstructure of a composite material.

summary_zh.method: 采用选区激光熔化制备并后续热处理。
summary_zh.result: 复合材料硬度与压缩强度显著提高。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微组织和力学测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to enhance the mechanical properties of Ti6Al4V by in-situ reinforcing with TiB2 via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Ti6Al4V-TiB2 composite samples were fabricated by selective laser melting and subsequently subjected to heat treatment.
summary_en.result: The composite exhibited improved hardness and compressive strength compared to unreinforced Ti6Al4V.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization and mechanical testing (hardness, compression) were performed to validate the reinforcement effect.

papers.title: Osteoinductive micro-nano guided bone regeneration membrane for in situ bone defect repair.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biomaterials used in bone tissue engineering must fulfill the requirements of osteoconduction, osteoinduction, and osseointegration. However, biomaterials with good osteoconductive properties face several challenges, including inadequate vascularization, limited osteoinduction and barrier ability, as well as the potential to trigger immune and inflammatory responses. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop guided bone regeneration membranes as a crucial component of tissue engineering strategies for repairing bone defects. METHODS: The mZIF-8/PLA membrane was prepared using electrospinning technology and simulated body fluid external mineralization method. Its ability to induce biomimetic mineralization was evaluated through TEM, EDS, XRD, FT-IR, zeta potential, and wettability techniques. The biocompatibility, osteoinduction properties, and osteo-immunomodulatory effects of the mZIF-8/PLA membrane were comprehensively evaluated by examining cell behaviors of surface-seeded BMSCs and macrophages, as well as the regulation of cellular genes and protein levels using PCR and WB. In vivo, the mZIF-8/PLA membrane's potential to promote bone regeneration and angiogenesis was assessed through Micro-CT and immunohistochemical staining. RESULTS: The mineralized deposition enhances hydrophilicity and cell compatibility of mZIF-8/PLA membrane. mZIF-8/PLA membrane promotes up-regulation of osteogenesis and angiogenesis related factors in BMSCs. Moreover, it induces the polarization of macrophages towards the M2 phenotype and modulates the local immune microenvironment. After 4-weeks of implantation, the mZIF-8/PLA membrane successfully bridges critical bone defects and almost completely repairs the defect area after 12-weeks, while significantly improving the strength and vascularization of new bone. CONCLUSIONS: The mZIF-8/PLA membrane with dual osteoconductive and immunomodulatory abilities could pave new research paths for bone tissue engineering.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及骨修复膜，但未涉及LPBF增材制造、应力遮挡或疲劳力学测试。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no stress shielding or stiffness matching analysis, no as-built surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发兼具骨传导和免疫调节功能的引导骨再生膜。
summary_zh.method: 通过静电纺丝和模拟体液矿化制备mZIF-8/PLA膜。
summary_zh.result: 膜促进成骨和血管化，12周后几乎完全修复骨缺损。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验及大鼠颅骨缺损模型体内验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a guided bone regeneration membrane with both osteoconductive and immunomodulatory properties for repairing critical-sized bone defects.
summary_en.method: An mZIF-8/PLA membrane was fabricated via electrospinning followed by simulated body fluid mineralization.
summary_en.result: The membrane promoted osteogenesis and angiogenesis in vitro and achieved near-complete bone defect repair with improved strength and vascularization after 12 weeks in vivo.
summary_en.validation: In vitro assays with BMSCs and macrophages, and in vivo rat calvarial defect model with Micro-CT and histological analysis.
